Regulatory trace

Controls shaping this journey

Control-family IDs resolve to the canonical India regulatory register.

RBI-DL-2025

Digital journey conduct, borrower disclosure, direct fund flow, servicing and recovery accountability.

RBI-KYC-2016

Customer identification, CDD, beneficial-owner and ongoing due-diligence evidence gate the relationship.

DPDP-2023

Purpose-bound notice, consent/other lawful basis, minimisation and data-principal rights govern personal data.

RBI-KFS-2024

APR, charges, repayment schedule and pre-contract terms must be delivered and evidenced before execution.

RBI-FUND-FLOW

Disbursement and repayment must use authorised direct flows; an LSP cannot control borrower funds.

RBI-FPC-PENAL

Penal charges must be reasonable, disclosed and posted as charges rather than capitalised penal interest.

RBI-CIR-2025

Credit reporting events must be accurate, timely, reconcilable and corrected through a governed process.

End-to-end execution

The lifecycle, stage by stage

Common controls and product-specific mechanics stay connected.

01

Lifecycle stage

Contract and configuration

Canonical contract product-journey/education_loan v1; archetype education finance; facility term loan; security unsecured or collateral.

  • Tenant administration must bind entitlement, product policy/version, pricing/KFS, providers, staffed roles, accounting, content/language and release readiness before intake.
  • The contract checksum prevents a workspace or lifecycle from silently using a different schema.
02

Lifecycle stage

Capture, facts and evidence

Authorised borrower, partner, field, branch and staff channels render the contract schema.

  • Required facts are: student ref, co borrower refs, institution ref, course code, admission ref, admission verified, course cost paise, fee schedule ref, customer contribution paise, moratorium months.
  • Required evidence is: admission letter, institution verification, fee schedule, academic records, co borrower income evidence, visa evidence if applicable.
  • Drafts remain tenant-, actor-, channel-, contract- and version-bound; server validation rejects omitted, malformed, cross-tenant or stale material.
03

Lifecycle stage

Specialist assessment and credit decision

The specialist underwriting focus is student/co-borrower, institution/course, admission, fee schedule and moratorium.

  • Common India, consent, KYC/AML, fraud, affordability and product-policy gates still apply.
  • Facts enter deterministic policy with provenance; outcomes are approve, refer or decline.
  • Exceptions and material model influence require attributed human review, and the approving checker must be independent of the proposer.
04

Lifecycle stage

KFS, contract and disbursement

Approved terms flow through APR/charge validation, KFS render, digital delivery and acceptance, agreement packet and eSign evidence.

  • Disbursement uses institution-direct fee tranches against schedule and progress.
  • Contract evidence, beneficiary authority and dual control are mandatory; unavailable verification or an ambiguous provider effect holds the lifecycle rather than opening an LMS account.
05

Lifecycle stage

LMS, accounting and servicing

The account uses exact decimal-string minor units and double-entry idempotent posting across term_loan.principal, term_loan.interest, term_loan.fees and term_loan.suspense.

  • Specialist servicing includes academic progress, moratorium interest, tranche review and EMI conversion.
  • Schedule is contractual expectation; ledger is actual money.
  • Every provider settlement is reconciled before final allocation.
06

Lifecycle stage

Distress, recovery and closure

Overdue obligations derive DPD and classification before conduct-governed collections work.

  • Product policy controls hardship, restructure, settlement, recovery, write-off and cure.
  • Closure requires zero/settled economics, reporting updates, NOC and independently approved security/collateral release.
  • Cancellation never deletes history.

Trace and readiness

How to operate and prove it

System map

API, state and evidence map

Workspace capture projects through /journey-workspaces and the journey-application promotion boundary; specialist cases use /admin/specialist-journeys; common stage proposals/approvals use composed-journey routes.

  • Persist journey type, contract/schema/configuration checksum, actor/tenant/channel, specialist result, policy trace, proposal/checker, KFS/document hashes, disbursement reference, account/ledger IDs, tasks/escalations and audit hashes.
  • Product pause, identity revocation and ambiguous effects pause the composed lifecycle.

Readiness

Maturity and production boundary

Canonical support: Configurable pattern.

  • Implemented boundary: Institution/course/admission, co-borrower, moratorium and stage gates.
  • Remaining before production-ready: Institution validation and tenant E2E.
  • This lesson describes the complete target and current executable contract; it does not claim that a tenant has certified providers, configured policy, completed UAT, witnessed security/DR or current operating-effectiveness evidence.

Adverse paths

Complete case matrix

Open a case to see its trigger and required fail-closed outcome.

01Happy path+

TriggerAll contract facts/evidence, policy and independent approvals are current

System outcomeProgress monotonically through composed lifecycle; create exact accounting and audit lineage

02Policy decline+

TriggerEligibility, affordability, limit, LTV or specialist rule declines

System outcomeRecord reason/trace; prohibit KFS-contract-disbursement progression

03Missing or invalid evidence+

TriggerA required document, checksum, version or condition is absent/expired

System outcomeFail closed at the current stage; create visible exception/manual work

04Provider timeout+

TriggerA required external verification has no authoritative response

System outcomeRefer or hold; never convert timeout into a positive fact

05Replay or duplicate+

TriggerSame idempotency key/callback is resubmitted

System outcomeReturn prior result or reject changed content; never double post or double disburse

06Stale version+

TriggerContract, schema, product configuration or proposal version changed

System outcomeReject stale action; require re-evaluation against the current version

07Wrong tenant+

TriggerActor or object belongs to another tenant

System outcomeDeny without cross-tenant disclosure; retain safe security evidence

08Wrong role or self-approval+

TriggerActor lacks channel/role authority or maker equals checker

System outcomeDeny and preserve the pending proposal for an independent actor

09Revocation mid-work+

TriggerIdentity, staffing, product or provider authority is suspended

System outcomePause affected specialist/composed cases and create governed escalation

10Reconciliation mismatch+

TriggerProvider, bank, escrow, merchant or subledger totals disagree

System outcomePost nothing ambiguous; route suspense/manual reconciliation with exact amounts

11Accounting imbalance+

TriggerPrincipal, interest, fee or suspense journal does not balance

System outcomeReject the posting atomically and alert; business status cannot outrun accounting

12Delinquency+

TriggerA contractual amount remains overdue

System outcomeDerive DPD/classification, create conduct-governed collections work and retain cure/restructure paths

13Cancellation or cooling-off+

TriggerBorrower/product permits exit before or shortly after disbursement

System outcomeUnwind documents, provider/merchant funds and ledger according to policy; evidence every refund

14Closure+

TriggerEconomic balance, charges and required releases/reporting are complete

System outcomeDual-control release where secured; issue NOC and preserve immutable history

15Rollback or ambiguous effect+

TriggerA transition partially reaches an external system

System outcomePause for manual intervention; never guess whether money/security moved

16Audit replay+

TriggerReviewer supplies recorded facts, policy/bundle and versions

System outcomeReproduce the decision and verify hashes, actor lineage, documents and ledger

17Journey-specific adverse cases+

Triggervisa refusal, dropout, fee refund, institution fraud and moratorium extension

System outcomeApply the specialist contract, fail closed, surface the owner and retain resolution evidence
